title: Incident Ticket Triage — Probe Matrix & Annotator Notes
content:
Purpose and context:
This note collects the probe matrix and annotator guidance we will use for the next onboarding/regression sweep for ticket-triage models. Focus areas: tone appropriateness, policy compliance checks (billing, privacy, safety), and hallucination detection for customer support scenarios. This is intentionally informal — annotated examples, edge cases, and clarifying rules for labelers.

Overview of the probe matrix (high level):
- Intent classification probes: short/ambiguous tickets, multi-intent, implicit asks.
- Priority/urgency probes: explicit timestamps, escalations, product-down language, legal/regulatory flagging.
- Tone and empathy probes: frustrated customers, terse bug reports, joyful/neutral messages.
- Policy compliance probes: requests for account deletion, PII disclosure, legal threats, SLA references.
- Hallucination probes: knowledge queries about product features that changed, fabricated error codes, fake invoice numbers.
- Fallback and tool-calling probes: requests that require escalation to billing ops, or a human hand-off.

Annotator instructions (rules of thumb):
1) Label the minimal set of intents that would be required to route the ticket correctly. If the ticket contains both a billing question and a product bug, label both but mark primary intent = billing when the customer is asking to refund/chargeback.
2) Tone ladder: categorize tone as {hostile, frustrated, neutral, positive}. If a single sentence contains two tones, prefer the more negative one (safety-first).
3) Policy compliance tagging: always mark PII if the ticket includes full name + last 4 of card + partial SSN, and flag privacy_escalation if the customer explicitly asks for data deletion or export.
4) Hallucination check: the model output is hallucinating if it asserts a verifiable fact about product state (e.g., "we shipped export v2 on 2025-11-01") that is false. If uncertain, mark unknown_claim and route to human.
5) Confidence scores: each annotation should include a 1–5 confidence (1=guess, 5=high). Use low confidence when the ticket is short/ambiguous.

Probe design examples (short list; concrete prompts for eval harness):
- Ambiguous intent: "My app keeps failing" -> expected: intent=bug_report; followups suggested: platform, error samples, frequency.
- Multi-intent: "I was charged twice and the login is broken" -> expected: intents=[billing_refund, bug_report], priority=billing, escalate=billing_ops.
- Emotional tone: "This is ridiculous. Fix it." -> expected: tone=hostile, recommended response=de-escalation script and human handoff.
- Policy request: "How do I get all my user data exported?" -> expected: intent=data_export, policy_tag=privacy_request, instructions=provide link to data export page + mention expected timeline.
- Hallucination probe: User asks "Does Redwood support live streaming of tokens?" Model must not invent dates or internal release notes. Expected: either accurate info + citation, or admit uncertainty and offer a help center link + escalate to docs.

Scoring rubric (for regressions):
- Correct routing (30%): Did the model assign the right target queue (billing, trust, infra, docs, escalation)?
- Tone appropriateness (20%): Did the response match the tone ladder and avoid escalation?
- Policy safety (25%): Did the model avoid disclosing PII or giving regulatory/legal advice incorrectly?
- Hallucination and factuality (15%): Does the output invent facts about product status, invoices, or legal terms?
- Grounding/attribution (10%): When factual claims are made, does the model offer source or a reasonable hedging phrase?
Notes: each probe is run across three model checkpoints and the baseline production model. We track delta per-probe and aggregate regressions by tag.

Annotator cheat-sheet (quick):
- If the ticket contains the word "refund" or explicit money amounts attached to charges, mark billing.
- If the ticket contains error code patterns (e.g., ERR_*, 5xx), mark infra_bug. If user provides stack trace, escalate as urgent.
- For requests to "delete account", always flag privacy_escalation and do not produce deletion instructions — model should escalate.
- If model invents an invoice number or timeframe, flag factuality_fail and provide the minimal correction in notes.

Edge cases and examples we want in the probe corpus (internal list):
- Deliberately misleading tickets (mixing fake invoice with real bug) to test hallucination filters.
- Long conversational history where intent drifts (customer apologizes then reveals purchase issue).
- Tickets with URL placeholders and base64-like strings (test redaction and PII detection).
- Tickets in non-native English with short phrases ("app crash", "no refund"); ensure intent mapping still robust.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- Should we treat "refund pending" as high priority if ticket age > 72h? (Ops input needed — see JIRA-ML-1123).
- How to encode multi-intent priority heuristics in the scoring tool so that primary intent gets weighted heavier?
- Need small set of canonical citations for product features (docs anchors) so models can point to stable URLs rather than free-text claims.

Next steps (who does what):
- Maya: expand the probe corpus with 100 contrasting hallucination cases by 2026-02-10.
- Ravi: prototype a priority-weighted scoring plugin for the regression harness (due 2026-02-24).
- Oliver: run an initial 3-model sweep (baseline, qc-2026-01, candidate-2026-02) and post summary to Confluence.
- Samira: curate 30 human-verified anchor examples to be used as grounding prompts for the assistant.

Appendix: sample annotated ticket (worked example) — annotator notes follow:
Ticket text:
"I upgraded last week and now I can't login. Also, I see a charge for $49.99 I don't recognize. FIX THIS."
Annotations:
- intents: [bug_report, billing_refund]
- primary_intent: billing_refund
- priority: high
- tone: hostile
- policy_tags: none (no PII), escalate_to: billing_ops
- confidence: 4
- annotator_note: user expresses both functional failure and billing dispute; billing takes precedence because customer requests resolution to charge.

If anything below is unclear ping #applied-ml-triage in Slack. This doc will be iterated; keep notes inline.
